summary: Bristol, Hartford County, CT: a 1924 account names a tower on the Bryce cottage on South Mountain as the county's only lookout; Forest Lookouts marks it removed.

facts.status_note: Forest Lookouts marks the tower Removed; no date or method given

events.note: 1924 account quoted by Forest Lookouts: the only lookout in Hartford County was a tower on the Bryce cottage on South Mountain in Bristol

evidence.supports: in 1924 Hartford County had not been thoroughly covered by lookout stations
evidence.quote: Hartford County has not been thoroughly covered by lookout stations

evidence.supports: the county's only lookout was a tower at the Bryce cottage on South Mountain in Bristol
evidence.quote: There has been only one in the county, a tower on the Bryce cottage on South Mountain in Bristol.

evidence.supports: the 1924 account is titled The Work of a Forest Protective Association
evidence.quote: The Work of a Forest Protective Association

evidence.supports: the tower looked out over the county's western section, the area west of Talcott Mountain
evidence.quote: This overlooks the portion of the county west of the Talcott Mountain range.

evidence.supports: Forest Lookouts lists the tower as removed

notes_for_editor: Single secondary source. The 1924 text is known only through the Forest Lookouts quote, which gives a town and county but no street address. Record coordinates (from eastern_us_lookouts) are not checked against a second source. The firetower.org Connecticut list (read from cache at firetower.org/lookouts/us/CT, 8 registered sites) does not name South Mountain. No NHLR entry found in cache. Bristol Historical Society Facebook posts about a cross at Castle Rock on South Mountain appeared only in search results and were not read, so they are not used. Story is short because the evidence is thin.
